sources.title: OSM/Nominatim: building named Centersquare Phoenix PHX1 at this address

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 95 (Centersquare): operator market page separates PHX1, Phoenix proper, from PHX3, Mesa, and this row city field favors a PHX3 match though the registry inherited name says PHX1, both figures recorded, no single capacity or sqft figure asserted as confirmed for this row, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete, no address applied.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Centersquare. This session found that centersquaredc.com, the legacy domain matching this registry entire Centersquare operator bucket naming, now issues a live redirect to www.csquare.com, the operator current domain, confirmed directly this session. Csquare own site states it owns and operates data centers built over decades by developing, acquiring, integrating, and operating advanced data centers, without giving a specific founding or rebrand date on the pages fetched this session. Csquare own site, fetched this session, lists corporate headquarters at 3100 Olympus Blvd, Suite 510, Coppell, TX 75019, and states a current portfolio of 80 total data centers, about 3.5 million square feet, more than 500 MW of power capacity, and more than 36,000 cross connects, across 15 North American markets plus London. On at least two Csquare pages fetched this session, a customer facing portal link pointed to evoquedcs.my.site.com, suggesting some relationship to Evoque Data Center Solutions, though this session found no page stating the exact nature of that relationship, such as whether Centersquare or Csquare is a direct rebrand of Evoque or a separate successor. Separately, this registry also carries an unrelated Cyxtera operator bucket, not part of this batch, already documented by an earlier pass in this registry as tracing to the same May 2017 CenturyLink data center divestiture discussed in this session own Lumen Technologies research, and as acquired by Cologix in 2023 per Cologix own site. This session found no evidence connecting that Cyxtera and Cologix history to the Centersquare, Csquare, or Evoque names researched for this batch, so the two threads are treated as distinct and unconfirmed to be related. This registry also carries a separate Csquare operator bucket, not part of this batch, whose name is now confirmed by the redirect evidence above to very likely be the same current brand as the Centersquare bucket this batch covers, though this session did not merge or rename either bucket, flagging this as an open duplicate operator naming question for a future dedicated pass rather than resolving it unilaterally. This row is named in the registry as Centersquare, Phoenix, PHX1, Mesa, with a city field of Mesa, AZ. The operator own current market page for Phoenix, fetched this session, treats PHX1 and PHX3 as two separate facilities, describing PHX1 as ten minutes from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport and fifteen minutes from downtown Phoenix at 13.3 MW UPS capacity and 40,456 square feet of raised floor, and describing PHX3 as in Mesa, about ten miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport, at 17.3 MW utility power, 8 MW UPS and 11.5 MW generator, and 50,256 square feet of raised floor. Because this row own city field says Mesa and the operator page places PHX3, not PHX1, in Mesa, this session leans toward PHX3 as the more consistent current match for this row, but the registry own inherited name still says PHX1, so this session records both operator published figures in this reading rather than asserting a single confirmed number, and flags the PHX1 versus PHX3 naming question for a future researcher rather than silently picking one.
